- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 80+ values), then undercorrects or lags in subsequent days.
- Underestimates in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting mean reversion or failure to capture late-period momentum.
- Forecasts tend to be too smooth; fails to capture volatility clustering or sudden reversals in the true outcome.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — often underestimates or delays correction.
- Overconfidence in early forecast days; model often starts with high values that don’t align with true trend shifts.
- When history shows a strong upward trend, model overreacts with excessive upward bias, then fails to adjust as trend stabilizes.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, especially when history includes recent peaks — model doesn’t “reset” to baseline after peaks.
